**Largest documented bottleneck: owner review and admission.** This is the directly observed serial step, not a measured causal allocation of hours. The interval 2026-11-11T04:05:49.609285+00:00 to 2026-11-12T04:35:09.227377+00:00 contains 195.910262 authorized slot-hours, 20.724020 occupied and 175.186242 idle (89.42% idle). Admission-to-terminal occupancy is not CPU utilization. Six slots are idle at the inspection and no waiting card meets complete ready/admission review, against a sixteen-card buffer target. This remains a defect while commissioned work exists.

Cause durations were not separately logged and overlap. All 175.186242 idle slot-hours are therefore causally unallocated; no invented partition is presented. Owner review, complete-source dependencies, reader memory, identity storage and retained mood qualification/cost holds are the observed causes. EX1's integration recovery adds a documented interruption, without a separately measured allocation. The accounting starts at the previous actual boundary, so reporting time is not lost between days.

**Hypothesis.** Are completed evidence, corrections, costs, source integrity and remaining obligations recorded accurately?

**METHOD.** Authenticate the calendar marker, all Week 5 report/receipt bindings and exact ledger anchors; integrate native admission-to-terminal occupancy; inspect native identities, fresh progress, leases, resources, locks and watcher delivery. Compare current theory-file bytes with the prior complete errata verification. Copy existing complete claim wording without reinterpreting unfinished output.

**Found.** The November 11 reconciliation preserves completed evidence and theory filing; chess and the text-free export continue in CPU-only Gear 2, while owner admission and source/resource holds leave substantial capacity unused.

**Corrections first.** The new export supervision and continuation correction is fully documented in [the recovery record](EX1_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERY_20261111.md). Original failures and charges remain. ### S15-W5-RR1-ACTUAL-ATTEMPTS-20261111

Limited sensitivity: the below-minus-above contrasts see effects of about 0.070328 to 0.121334 or more; the inherited bar is 0.066281.

**Hypothesis.** Does the phone-game reference pattern persist across actual attempts when the first three attempts use the same returning people?

**METHOD.** Reuse the qualified MD3 participant-intercept logistic model and its original eight predictors, forgetting factor and common first-play scales. Select people with saved, unambiguous actual attempts 1, 2 and 3; fit each actual-attempt bin separately, retaining all observed fourth-and-later attempts. Compare score against the current play start and against the best observed earlier completed score. Use 2,000 whole-person bootstrap refits per applicable panel and a fresh independent replay of every required panel, draw and exclusion census.

**Found.** Within the fixed returning cohort, the game-start slopes change across observed attempts and the pattern also depends on the reference; this descriptive comparison does not establish learning or social standing.

The coefficient unit is log-odds of choosing the gamble per one original standing standard deviation (199.007134498631 score points). Below-reference standing is signed and nonpositive: a positive slope means less gambling farther below the reference; a negative slope means more gambling farther below it. Above-reference standing is nonnegative. The contrast is the below slope minus the above slope. Nuisance predictors are trial type (gain/loss indicators), the gamble's expected-value advantage, earlier gamble count, trial index and discounted recent outcomes; forgetting remains 0.65. All scales remain the original global first-play scales rather than being refitted within bins.

The table retains every fitted coefficient of interest. Intervals are 95% whole-person percentile bootstrap intervals; SE is the standard deviation of its 2,000 saved draws. The bar is the original MD3 first-play threshold, shown as an inherited yardstick rather than a newly calibrated decision rule for these panels. Sees is 2.8 times SE; supports at is bar plus 2.8 times SE. Both are approximate, somewhat optimistic normal-model benchmarks, not empirical power measurements; the latter column does not confer a supported verdict. Every row is a descriptive configured re-read, including rows whose intervals exclude zero or clear the inherited bar.

Best-observed-earlier-score at actual attempt 1 is **not applicable**: no earlier completed play exists. The 5,167 people and plays in that entry have no high-score coefficient or interval. This is structural unavailability, not zero, an unsupported fit or a scientific null. All seven applicable fits converge, all 2,000 draws per fit are finite and nondegenerate, and every informative-person count exceeds 20. No failed draw is dropped or replaced; the below-floor fallback was not used.

**Cohort and missing records.** The source has 47,067 people and 91,046 saved plays. Of these, 7,237 people have at least three saved plays (42,986 plays); 39,830 have fewer than three. Among the former, 2,068 lack at least one required actual counter and three have ambiguous histories. These categories overlap and must not be added as disjoint exclusions. Missing actual attempt 1 affects 928 people, missing 2 affects 894, and missing 3 affects 987; these counts also overlap. The accepted full cohort is 5,167 people, with 30,988 saved plays; no prospective population sample was needed. The difference of 2,070 people between the eligible-by-saved-count set and the accepted cohort is the distinct exclusion count, not the sum of overlapping categories. Source counters include attempted plays that may have no saved completed record. We neither renumber available records nor impute choices or scores.

The next table gives actual people and completed plays before fitting, and people whose choices vary enough to inform the grouped model. Counts are the same for both references where both apply. Fourth-and-later contains all such observed plays, not one fourth play per person.

Fixed entry holds composition constant for attempts 1/2/3 before fit-specific nonconstant-choice exclusions; it does not remove fourth-and-later selection, missing-history bias or changing effective fit populations.

**Means and theory return.** In the fixed cohort, first-attempt play-start estimates again have a positive below slope and an above interval inside the inherited practical band. At attempts 2 and 3, the lower slopes remain positive while above-reference slopes are negative. In fourth-and-later plays both slopes are negative. Against best observed earlier score the lower interval crosses zero at attempts 2 and 3; both slopes are negative in the fourth-and-later subset. All fitted below-minus-above intervals are positive, but a positive contrast alone is not a floor-only signature: negative slopes and reference choice matter. The best-earlier repeat panels must not be pooled with or substituted for the original MD3 repeat result.

This is a sequence of separate fits, not a jointly tested between-attempt difference or causal learning effect. Shared people and seed streams do not turn the recorded marginal intervals into a registered interaction test. No normal approximation here resolves a unique kink, smooth-value mechanism or adaptation process. The G241/G257 security distinction, November 7 correction and H12-T6 floor-versus-ladder question concern more than a game-score proxy; neither social standing, rank striving, other needs nor their balance is measured. The preserved theory wording and afterword were reread. This result informs the internal Round 12 return without changing canonical theory standing or earlier verdicts.

### S15-W5-SP3-IC-20261110

**Hypothesis.** Could the original thermal-distance comparison detect the predeclared practical effect under the observed building design?

**METHOD.** Reconstruct the exact completed parent source and original building summaries. Retain all 213 eligible buildings in each bootstrap draw, then select the 51 weather-linked naturally ventilated buildings for the original ordinary least-squares contrast. For each coefficient, generate 100 worlds and all 2,000 original full-frame bootstrap draws. Authenticate both original 25-world pilot boundaries and require fresh native reconstruction of all 500 worlds and every numeric draw array.

**Found.** Under the fixed observed building design, the thermal-distance comparison has limited sensitivity at the registered practical effect; the inconclusive human primary cannot establish absence.

The table reports the complete conditional calibration. Coefficients and estimate-distribution quantiles are changes in sensation-per-degree slope per outdoor-distance degree. Distribution quantiles describe variation across constructed worlds; they are not an interval for the human primary. Coverage is the fraction of worlds whose bootstrap interval contains its planted coefficient. Zero exclusion is in the planted direction, and is two-sided for the null. The last column applies the original primary's negative-support rule, whose interval must lie below minus 0.01; it is distinct from detecting a nonzero planted effect.

| Planted coefficient | Estimate distribution, 2.5% / median / 97.5% | 95% interval coverage | Expected-direction zero exclusion | Original negative-support classification |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| -0.02 | -0.03790712 / -0.02212712 / -0.00402299 | 0.96 | 0.54 | 0.18 |
| -0.01 | -0.02790712 / -0.01212712 / 0.00597701 | 0.96 | 0.18 | 0.02 |
| +0.00 | -0.01790712 / -0.00212712 / 0.01597701 | 0.96 | 0.04 | 0.00 |
| +0.01 | -0.00790712 / 0.00787288 / 0.02597701 | 0.96 | 0.09 | 0.00 |
| +0.02 | 0.00209288 / 0.01787288 / 0.03597701 | 0.96 | 0.38 | 0.00 |

The null exclusion rate is 0.04, within the frozen maximum of 0.10. The negative and positive one-bar detection rates are 0.18 and 0.09, both below the required 0.80. The joint sensitivity criterion therefore fails. All 500 worlds and all draws are retained, with no failed draws. This is a completed calibration outcome, not an engineering failure to heal, a support-floor failure or a result-dependent reason to reduce the grid.

**Scope and parent interpretation.** The source contains 42,007 responses in 567 buildings; the original exclusion removes 354 buildings with fewer than 30 responses, leaving the 213-building sampling frame. The analytic weather-linked subset is 51 buildings. The simulated outcomes condition on estimated building slopes, observed weather distances and sign-symmetric residual magnitudes. They do not estimate general population power under other noise laws, within-person thermal adaptation, a causal set-point mechanism or a human effect of opposite sign. The original observational result (S15-W5-SP3-20261107) remains inconclusive. It must now be accompanied by limited conditional sensitivity at the practical bar, rather than interpreted as evidence of no dulling. No p-value is introduced.

### OPS-S15-W5-WAKE-BACKPRESSURE-20261109

**Hypothesis.** Can the watcher stop redundant queued turns while preserving every result and the existing event and inactivity policy?

**METHOD.** Inspect the native pending queue and durable event database; reproduce acknowledgment-before-consumption, overlapping sends, active-owner bursts and deletion recovery with disposable queues. Change only notification delivery, record pending research outputs fully, retire only byte-verified fully acknowledged messages, and verify the restarted watcher's native identity and loaded source hashes.

**Found.** Operational wakes now wait for the active turn and pending app message to clear; acknowledged stale messages are retired without discarding results.

The old guard waited only for unacknowledged local events. Recording a result before its queued message was consumed cleared that guard and allowed another message to accumulate. Urgent messages also bypassed the active-owner check. The native inspection found two pending watcher messages: an already recorded resource pause and a completed reader continuation. That continuation was fully authenticated and written through before acknowledgment. Both exact acknowledged messages were then retired and the native inventory verified empty. The user's deleted notifications did not remove the local event records or these authenticated result files. The exact contents of previously deleted app entries cannot be reconstructed from the surviving inventory alone; no deletion is treated as scientific acknowledgment.

The repaired watcher uses an active-owner barrier for all operational events, a kernel-held send lock and a native-queue barrier independent of local acknowledgment. Later events collect durably for a combined wake. Exact stale acknowledged messages are removed only after matching their event IDs, complete generated text and stable batch identity, followed by a fresh queue check. Ordinary user messages, changed messages and partially acknowledged batches remain. A queued but unacknowledged event missing from the app gets two separated observations and a one-minute delivery-hook grace period; only an idle owner with no consumption receipt permits transport recovery. Actual delivery is recorded even for an already acknowledged result. An inspection failure prevents further dispatch; ambiguous sends remain visible.

All 225 targeted watcher, queue, acknowledgment-race, lifecycle, transition, scheduling and inactivity checks pass, including nine new backpressure cases. The initial test invocation hit environment setup errors in its default temporary location and was interrupted; the complete targeted run passed using an explicit workspace temporary directory with the pytest cache disabled. The production watcher was restarted by its identified helper only; its source, queue transport and common-module hashes match the reviewed files. Native queue retirement and the active-owner suppression decision are directly observed. No synthetic wake or new model turn was sent to test delivery. The complete future event lifecycle remains subject to its next real event, distinct from the tested and observed behaviors above.

V1 continuation 37's checkpoint and the original reader's ordinal 34 completion are separately recorded and acknowledged. V1 continuation 38 is admitted under unchanged scope and limits; the next original reader chunk awaits fresh resource admission. The full pilot and bank remain unfinished. Research settings, result bytes, original time windows, CPU-only Gear 2 and resource guards are unchanged. Events and four hours of owner inactivity remain the schedule; no periodic model checks are added. The ready buffer remains deficient because owner qualification and admission are unfinished, with original builders delivered/inactive.

**Means.** Stop stacking redundant operational turns while keeping evidence and recovery durable. Continue commissioned work and apply full write-through before every ACK. No new scientific test is harvested from this operational instruction; no gear, spending, GPU, Ollama or delegation authority is added. Final scientific reporting remains under the active packet.

### S15-W5-LA2-ICSI-20261107

**Hypothesis.** Do ICSI speakers with the same recorded English variety or region join each other’s laughter more often?

**METHOD.** Separately project the two recorded metadata fields onto every participant pair, count missing metadata and undefined no-laugh fractions, and calculate the symmetric share of laugh onsets joined within one second. Regress each share on same versus different recorded background and both speakers’ base laugh rates with within-meeting centering. Refit 2,000 whole-meeting bootstrap draws for each frozen comparison.

**Found.** Both ICSI background comparisons are inconclusive; recorded English variety and region do not establish a shared-inference mechanism.

The table reports each distinct background construct, the number of analytical meetings and pairs, its same-minus-different coefficient in joined-laugh share units, and its meeting-cluster 95% interval. Both use the prospectively fixed 0.02 practical bar.

| Recorded background | Meetings | Pairs | Coefficient | 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Recorded English variety | 75 | 999 | 0.00956351 | [-0.00186308, 0.02133276] |
| Recorded region | 64 | 215 | -0.01129047 | [-0.04261036, 0.02422023] |

The complete metadata source has 1,466 possible participant pairs in 75 meetings. English variety supports 999 pairs and leaves 467 unsupported. Region supports 215 and leaves 1,251 unsupported; these supported pairs occur in 64 analytical meetings. Unknown values and undefined event fractions remain counted exclusions, never zero effects.

Neither establishes absence, equivalence or a causal background effect. English variety and region are separate recorded constructs, neither a declaration of native language, nationality or the proposed shared internal model. Familiarity, roles and shared experience remain unmeasured. Meeting resampling preserves within-meeting dependence but does not randomize background or account for every repeated-speaker relation across meetings. Signed/null numerical controls, the actual-format metadata projection fixture and complete independent replay pass; minimum-effect sensitivity in the observed designs remains to be quantified. No new p-value is introduced.

### S15-TD-B4-EFFORT-SKILL-20261106

**Hypothesis.** Does additional deliberation improve move quality more for stronger chess players, as a proxy test of the curator's effect-equals-effort-times-power conjecture?

**METHOD.** Use the frozen one-percent game draw from the complete April 2017 Lichess month, retaining games with clock and engine-evaluation annotations and moves passing the source checks. Model negative centipawn loss on standardized rating, log seconds and their standardized product, with phase and absolute prior evaluation as declared controls. Instrument time and its rating product using a prior clock at most ten seconds and its rating product. Report ordinary least squares beside the two-stage diagnostic. Recompute both stages in 2,000 game-cluster bootstrap draws and independently replay the complete calculation. Constructed positive, negative and null fixtures and independent two-stage arithmetic preceded the run.

**Found.** The registered chess effort-by-skill diagnostic is inconclusive; the ordinary regression association does not establish that effort and power multiply causally.

The table reports the coefficient on the standardized interaction, in centipawns, with game-cluster percentile intervals. Higher quality means less centipawn loss. The primary supports only when its entire interval exceeds +1, counts against the proxy prediction when its entire interval is at or below zero, and is otherwise inconclusive.

| Model | Product coefficient | 95% interval | Role |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Low-clock instrument diagnostic | -2.498420 | [-15.897875, 11.944513] | Primary: inconclusive |
| Ordinary regression | 2.522756 | [1.253713, 3.761304] | Descriptive companion |

The sample has 9912 usable games and 514787 moves, exceeding the frozen 1,000-game and 10,000-move floors. Both model matrices have full rank. The excluded-instrument partial F statistics are 9708.616868 and 8416.349592, above the frozen ten-point numerical gate. All 2000 bootstrap draws have valid numerical fits; none are dropped. The point-fit strength gate passes. Bootstrap draws with weaker but nonsingular instruments are retained under the implementation; this record does not assert that every resample passes the point-fit strength gate.

Instrument strength does not establish exclusion. Low remaining time can directly impair decisions, and hard positions can both use time and worsen play. Absolute prior evaluation is an incomplete difficulty control. The ordinary regression and instrumental diagnostic have different signs and uncertainty; the companion cannot replace the registered primary after outcomes. Rating is an imperfect skill proxy and elapsed seconds is an imperfect effort proxy. These observations therefore neither identify causal effort nor prove or refute the general multiplicative conjecture.

The one-percent draw precedes annotation filtering, but the analysis sample is annotation-dependent. One-second clock precision excludes nonpositive measured elapsed times; mate evaluations are excluded rather than converted into centipawns. Game clustering conditions on the sampled games and observed players. Repeated players across games and unknown cross-game dependence are not modeled, so this is not new-player population uncertainty. Complete source counts and dispositions remain in B4_SOURCE.md. No usernames, game identifiers or raw moves enter public artifacts. Source: [Lichess CC0 database](https://database.lichess.org/).

A valid-null or inconclusive scientific gate is not an engineering failure and is not healed.

### S15-TD-B2-REFUSALS-20261106

**Hypothesis.** At equal numbers of observed dilemmas, do more returning Moral Machine choosers always choose the same side of species or intervention than of gender or fitness?

**METHOD.** Use the complete authenticated all-session archive after source admission. Keep the common cohort with at least two sessions and at least three valid paired scenarios on each of four dimensions. Within each fingerprint, draw the same number of scenarios from each dimension, equal to its minimum dimension count, without replacement and with seed 20261106. A hypergeometric draw of binary-choice counts is equivalent to drawing those scenarios. Compare the mean never-trading indicator across species and intervention against the mean across gender and fitness. Compute a 2,000-draw fingerprint-cluster percentile interval, retain all component rates, and compare all-observed rates with the fair-coin expectation at their original counts. Signed and null arithmetic fixtures and a complete literal source fixture precede this run; the full analysis independently replays.

**Found.** At matched exposure, the pooled species-and-intervention never-trading rate exceeds gender-and-fitness in this returning-fingerprint cohort; this does not identify terminal identity.

The common cohort contains 301689 fingerprints. The pooled difference is 14.509147 percentage points, with a 95% fingerprint-bootstrap interval of [14.370420, 14.653667]. The entire interval exceeds the precommitted five-percentage-point practical bar, so the frozen pooled rule returns supports. This is a descriptive result in the selected common cohort, not a population prevalence estimate or a causal identity result.

Every number in the table is a percentage of the same common cohort, except the last column, which is the mean expected percentage for independent fair choices at each fingerprint's original dimension count. Equal exposure uses the same number of choices across dimensions within a fingerprint. All observed uses each dimension's full available history. Neither column includes the marginal dimension-only cohorts reported at source admission.

| Dimension | Equal-exposure never trading (%) | All-observed never trading (%) | All-observed fair-coin expectation (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Species | 51.231235 | 48.366364 | 9.37531266 |
| Intervention | 14.549420 | 0.136896 | 0.00012888 |
| Gender | 17.942650 | 14.447660 | 9.44425464 |
| Fitness | 18.819712 | 17.873041 | 11.93758377 |

Species and intervention do not individually show the same ordering: species has the largest equal-exposure never-trading rate, while intervention falls below both mundane dimensions. The pooled support therefore must not be restated as separate support for each named component. No component significance test was performed here. The contrast does not distinguish protected values from stable ordinary preferences or choices induced by the offered scenarios. The fair-coin benchmark is deliberately weak: a stable unequal ordinary preference can also exceed it. It is not a calibrated model of ordinary preference heterogeneity.

Fingerprint linkage does not prove person identity, and returning fingerprints with sufficient coverage form a selected population. The same person can have multiple fingerprints and a fingerprint can be shared. The interval treats the observed fingerprint as its cluster; it does not account for an unknown linkage map. Its primary uncertainty is conditional on the fixed matching, source release and seeded subset scheme. The source's prior release filtering and the broad intervention comparison remain limits. No present endorsement, satiation, contingency-degradation response, or refusal of an unobserved offer was measured. The curator's learned-end distinction remains open.

All-observed rates and coin expectations here refer explicitly to the common cohort. Source-admission counts for all dimension-eligible fingerprints remain separately recorded; they are not substituted into these denominators. No raw choices, fingerprint identifiers, demographic fields or source text are published. Attribution: Awad et al. (2018), The Moral Machine experiment, [CC-BY source](https://osf.io/3hvt2/).

**Means.** Retain the scoped pooled result and its component asymmetry, without converting finite repeated choice into proof of terminal identity. Register B2.s, B2.m and B2.p as first-generation follow-ups, each capped at 3,600 CPU seconds and subject to the original campaign allowance and deadlines. Freeze designs and validate before execution; follow-ups register no descendants.

- B2.s: Check dependence on exposure: freeze a specification comparison of exactly three choices per dimension and the original within-fingerprint minimum, without changing the common cohort or original result.
- B2.m: Separate the pooled result into species and intervention contrasts against the same mundane-dimension mean; test whether the component pattern explains the pooled contrast rather than assuming both components agree.
- B2.p: Replace the single uniform subset draw with the exact hypergeometric expectation of never-trading for each fingerprint and dimension; compare against the original to check subset-randomness sensitivity.

**Hypothesis.** Do disagreements between independent raters preferentially substitute words assigned to the same proposed channel?

**METHOD.** Count exclusive-label disagreements over ordered distinct-rater pairs on each clear comment. Divide by the count expected from rating marginals, and compare each of six assigned pairs against its strongest supported cross-channel rival. Recompute marginals in 2,000 comment-cluster draws. Retain the full-data fixed competitor, add a maximum-reselected companion, compare unassigned categories separately, and repeat on exactly-three-rater comments. Exact scalar counts and an independent-label factorial null validate the arithmetic before human execution.

**Found.** The registered within-channel disagreement comparison remains inconclusive; its complete sensitivity check is limited in balanced constructed worlds and does not establish human-population power (S15-TD5-IC-SENSITIVITY-20261106).

The full primary contains 57,349 comments, 209,971 ratings and 607,458 ordered pairs. The exactly-three-rater companion contains 37,335 comments, 112,005 ratings and 224,010 ordered pairs. Both return the packet's inconclusive outcome: two cross-channel wins, two losses and two unresolved pairs. The against rule requires at least three losses; support requires all six wins. The frozen practical difference is 0.1 lift units in the declared direction.

Each row is a declared pair compared with its strongest cross-channel rival. Difference is within-pair lift minus rival lift. Brackets are 95% comment-bootstrap intervals, conditional on this corpus and annotation allocation; the second interval reselects the maximum within the same eligible competitor pool on each draw.

| Population | Pair | Fixed rival | Difference | Fixed interval | Reselected interval | Decision |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| primary | anger / annoyance | anger / disgust | -0.0809312 | [-0.258341, 0.101728] | [-0.258341, 0.101728] | inconclusive |
| primary | fear / nervousness | nervousness / sadness | 2.76959 | [1.97824, 3.54409] | [1.93931, 3.47914] | win |
| primary | grief / sadness | nervousness / sadness | 2.89998 | [2.16741, 3.66237] | [2.16741, 3.66237] | win |
| primary | amusement / joy | excitement / joy | -0.116395 | [-0.324439, 0.0924209] | [-0.324439, 0.0924209] | inconclusive |
| primary | curiosity / excitement | excitement / joy | -1.3128 | [-1.50132, -1.12226] | [-1.50132, -1.12226] | loss |
| primary | caring / love | caring / nervousness | -1.01221 | [-1.29957, -0.735765] | [-1.30106, -0.871336] | loss |
| exactly_three | anger / annoyance | anger / disgust | 0.12683 | [-0.245979, 0.502482] | [-0.245979, 0.502482] | inconclusive |
| exactly_three | fear / nervousness | disgust / fear | 3.19955 | [1.66478, 4.8733] | [1.66478, 4.8733] | win |
| exactly_three | grief / sadness | fear / sadness | 3.94075 | [2.51851, 5.45196] | [2.48114, 5.41974] | win |
| exactly_three | amusement / joy | excitement / joy | -0.105813 | [-0.404167, 0.207809] | [-0.404167, 0.207809] | inconclusive |
| exactly_three | curiosity / excitement | excitement / joy | -1.35923 | [-1.63064, -1.07823] | [-1.63064, -1.07823] | loss |
| exactly_three | caring / love | joy / love | -0.954194 | [-1.12297, -0.781733] | [-1.12297, -0.781733] | loss |

Against unassigned categories, the full-data comparisons win for anger/annoyance and fear/nervousness, are unresolved for grief/sadness, and lose for amusement/joy, curiosity/excitement and caring/love. The exactly-three-rater comparison instead wins for amusement/joy. All unassigned estimates, intervals and expected counts are in the aggregate JSON receipt. These comparisons are separate because the theory treats unassigned categories as mixtures.

The six primary pairs include sparse within-channel expected counts even where their rival passes the 50-count floor. The packet applies that floor to competitors, not to the within-channel pair. A reselected maximum bootstrap is a sensitivity calculation, not guaranteed valid post-selection inference near tied maxima. The comment bootstrap holds the observed rater pool fixed and does not estimate generalization to new raters. The original arithmetic null checks did not establish power. The complete first-generation calibration now shows limited full-rule sensitivity and poor interval coverage under its balanced single-label construction (S15-TD5-IC-SENSITIVITY-20261106), without establishing human-population power. This inconclusive human result is not evidence of channel equivalence or absence. Everyday emotion labels need not identify inherited functions.

**Means.** Keep the mixed pair pattern and the aggregate inconclusive outcome. Retain the completed instrument sensitivity check and its construction limits; do not tune the mappings after these outcomes.

### S15-TD4-WORD-SCALES-20261106

**Hypothesis.** Do the curator's ordered emotion words behave as single increasing scales in independent human word norms?

**METHOD.** Apply the frozen words and emotion mappings to NRC Emotion Intensity v1 and VAD v2.1, with no stemming, synonyms or added zero scores. Require four covered words. Count adjacent inversions and rank correlation; fit dominance linearly on mapped intensity (arousal for LUST) and divide its residual standard deviation by arousal's standard deviation. Validate constructed straight, reversed, off-line and degenerate cases before the real run; reparse and recompute every result independently in a fresh process.

**Found.** The specified PLAY word order fails the frozen word-norm rule; four covered scales are inconclusive and three lack the required intensity coverage. These norms do not identify biological channels.

The table shows each declared scale, its number of intensity-covered words (arousal-covered words for LUST), adjacent reversals, rank correlation, the off-line residual ratio and the precommitted verdict. Correlation 1 means exact increasing rank order; the ratio is a linear-shape diagnostic. It is not an interval or a measure of a neural dimension.

| Scale | Covered words | Adjacent inversions | Rank correlation | Off-line ratio | Verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| CARE | 3 | not available | not available | not available | design cannot test |
| DISGUST | 3 | not available | not available | not available | design cannot test |
| FEAR | 5 | 0 | 1 | 0.778331 | inconclusive |
| LUST | 4 | 0 | 1 | 0.550768 | inconclusive |
| PANIC/GRIEF | 4 | 1 | 0.8 | 0.509329 | inconclusive |
| PLAY | 5 | 2 | -0.3 | 0.309556 | against |
| RAGE | 6 | 1 | 0.942857 | 0.968449 | inconclusive |
| SEEKING | 3 | not available | not available | not available | design cannot test |

All declared words are available in VAD. Missing intensity scores leave SEEKING, CARE and DISGUST with three words each; those scales cannot test the registered joint criterion. CARE's joy companion has two covered words and SEEKING's joy companion three, also below the floor. Coverage masks in the aggregate receipt refer to positions in the already-public curator lists; no raw lexicon entries or wordwise norm values are published. The covered PLAY list has two reversals, meeting the against rule independently of its low residual ratio. The other four covered primary lists meet neither decisive band. No scale meets both the no-inversion and ratio-below-0.5 support rule.

### S15-CA5-R-H1-20261026

**Hypothesis.** Do a person's joke-topic preferences recur across different jokes after accounting for joke popularity and that person's general rating tendency?

**METHOD.** An exact program compared topic profiles across odd- and even-numbered jokes for all 50,691 approved complete Jester records, using 1,728,830 observed ratings. Eight lexical topics were frozen from all 150 complete joke texts before rating outcomes; one text without learned topic loading retains uniform weights under the separately frozen correction. Separate least-squares person and item effects on each half's actual observed cells remove additive rating generosity and popularity. Correlation measures how similarly a person's topic departures vary across halves, from minus one for opposite profiles to one for matching profiles; the primary equally weights persons and subtracts the rebuilt reference mean.

The full comparison uses 1,000 within-item residual reassignments and 200 within-person outcome reassignments, rebuilding the additive fit and profiles for each reassignment. Its 2,000 paired-person bootstrap samples resample the resulting real and mean-reference correlations with the fitted population adjustment fixed. Missing cells stay missing; no rater is dropped and no rating is imputed. Every source, feature, known-answer check and statistic was reconstructed in a fresh native process before this landing.

The table compares the same real-person mean correlation with two separately rebuilt references. The reference band is its 2.5th to 97.5th percentile across draws. The excess and its 95% interval use paired real-person resampling. Probabilities are one-sided descriptive permutation values, not multiplicity-adjusted confirmation.

| Comparison | Real mean | Reference mean / standard deviation | Reference 95% band | Excess over reference [95% paired interval] | Descriptive probability |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| Primary: residuals reassigned among people within each joke | 0.024669 | 0.000034 / 0.002009 | [-0.003950, 0.004050] | 0.024636 [0.020876, 0.028524] | 0.000999001 |
| Outcome control: residuals reassigned within each person and half | 0.024669 | 0.000135 / 0.002025 | [-0.004068, 0.004038] | 0.024534 [0.020726, 0.028473] | 0.004975124 |

**Found.** Supports small joke-topic preference recurrence beyond additive person and item averages in the approved Jester records; this descriptive conditional comparison does not establish demographic-relative harm judgments or value recovery.

The full result is positive under the frozen conjunction of a positive lower interval endpoint and a primary permutation probability below .05. Neither reference triggers the inherited mean-bias warning: each mean is less than a quarter of its reference standard deviation. All 50,691 records remain, with no constant profiles. The ten unrated items remain in the text census and do not acquire invented ratings. The within-person reference is an outcome control, not a second independent dataset.

The validation table reports known constructed answers using the real exposure mask, not additional empirical effects. The null gate is exact for additive person/item effects; the noise gate concerns the mean of twenty fixed worlds, not absence of every individual false alarm.

## Corrections first

- **control**: Literal leave-writer-out context can encode a negative fingerprint of the omitted writer. Its complete results are diagnostic only and cannot license badges, even where both numerical gates pass.
- **scope**: WA0.h1 is the curator-approved independent-donor successor on a separately declared session-summary estimand and smaller fixed galleries. Original pooled results and failed old reference flags remain unchanged.
- **arithmetic**: GEN1 marginal totals do not identify paired discordance. Retain measured joint tables and exact planning grids; remove the unsupported universal 31-point sensitivity assertion for this rebuilt design.

## Primary and route

The approved h1 primary passes both gates: residualized final-document habit identification is 0.422222, context 0, difference 0.422222 [0.266667, 0.577778], one-sided empirical p=0.000999001. The raw habit arm also passes. The literal diagnostic has no badge licence regardless of its numerical gates.

Human CoAuthor source records and mixed human/model final documents; exact nearest-neighbour program over frozen features. All 1,399 original sessions and 990 genre-matched sessions are retained. Identification probes retain 45 eligible writers, each tested once against a fixed 30-writer gallery. Genre probes retain all 24 writers, each tested once against 16. The estimates are descriptive and conditional on those galleries and features; intervals resample probe writers, not galleries. No psychological automaticity, causal mechanism, private preference or general population identification claim follows.

The new session-summary variant uses unweighted session-feature means in real, context and permuted arms. Whole prompts, ordered by first timestamp within writer, alternate between disjoint halves. In three frozen writer-role rotations, independent donor writers supply same-prompt context means; each writer is a probe once. One common writer-label assignment is shuffled within prompt and role fold for each of 1,000 draws and reused across rotations. Accepted-share nuisance coefficients are fit using gallery sessions only and refit in every null draw. The pass rule is one-sided empirical p<0.05 and a positive lower bound for the 2,000-draw paired probe-writer 95% interval. Page routes additionally require both raw and residualized variants to pass.

Both raw and residualized final-document style pass. All six complete PMAP process channels pass under h1; content remains unsupported. Typed fragments remain auxiliary. These are conditional identification results, without a causal habit or automaticity interpretation.

### S15-CA5

**Hypothesis.** A person's pattern of perceived harm judgments recurs across different items after shared demographic responses and overall severity are removed.
**METHOD.** Use all 123 released DICES raters and 350 items, subtract the leave-one-rater-out gender-by-race group/item mean, and separately center each person's odd/even-item half. Correlate each person's profiles across 36 harm topics present in both halves. Compare the mean with 1,000 itemwise writer-label permutations within demographic groups; use 2,000 paired-rater bootstrap draws. Repeat on the published 104-person quality subset and reconstruct the complete calculation in a fresh native process.
**Found.** The topic-specific pattern recurs weakly but above the within-group reference in both the full population and published quality subset.
**Means.** This supports recurring personal disagreement about perceived harm in this corpus. It does not identify independent values, objective safety or competence.

The table reports the complete real-human comparison read by an exact program. Correlation runs from negative agreement to perfect agreement at 1; intervals resample raters, and the reference probability is the one-sided empirical tail from 1,000 reassignments. Both estimates are descriptive commissioned comparisons, not an independently replicated confirmatory claim.

| Population | Raters | Mean profile correlation |95% rater interval| Mean reassignment correlation |95% reference interval| Empirical probability |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| All released |123|0.139767|[0.105093,0.174035]|0.000036|[-0.034320,0.034560]|0.000999001|
| Published quality subset |104|0.133955|[0.096592,0.170797]|-0.000068|[-0.035626,0.037446]|0.000999001|

Both populations contain all 350 items. Thirty-six harm topics occur in both halves; 35 lack support in one half and do not define a shared profile coordinate. Every retained rater contributes, with no singleton-group or constant-profile exception. The full-population real-minus-reference contrast is 0.139731; the quality sensitivity is 0.134023. The score maps No to 0, Unsure to 0.5 and Yes to 1. The quality sensitivity follows the published 19-rater exclusion list; it does not replace the full population.

The descriptive full-population sum-of-squares partition is 239.936792 for demographic group, 1830.411823 for item, 469.098621 for item-by-group, 1444.843103 for rater within group, and 5236.393841 for item-by-rater plus unreplicated error, totaling 9220.684181. There is only one observation per rater/item, so the last term cannot separate interaction from noise. Recurrence across distinct items helps test persistence; it cannot turn this partition into independent value ground truth. ### S15-DRIVE-V4C-SPLIT-1018

**Hypothesis.** Learning a reader's feature choices on separate decisions makes its test for writer-specific taste distinguish planted structure from worlds with no such structure.
**METHOD.** Refit all 110 original constructed worlds, alternating decisions within each session into two halves. Learn feature directions, dimension, scaling and history settings on one half; freeze them, estimate only variance components on the other half, then swap and average the two marginal likelihood-ratio statistics. Separate causal histories prevent outcomes crossing the split. An exact numerical program compares taste features, history alone and their combination against the original zero-effect and shuffled-world gates.
**Found.** The taste and combined readers still fail their mandatory false-alarm gates. **Means.** The corrected split does not admit the primary taste reader. This is an instrument failure, not evidence that people lack taste or history-dependent behavior. The history-only reader meets the sampled null bands but detects taste reliably only at the largest planted strength; that narrower result does not admit the medium-strength route.

The same 20 shuffled worlds appear once per reader and are repeated across that reader's rows for comparison. A valid null gate allows at most one detection in ten zero-effect worlds and two in twenty shuffled worlds. The fixed labels require at least 80% medium-strength recovery for `sees`, or at least 80% large-strength recovery for `sees large only`, after passing those null gates.

examination. Nine writers lack both repertoire groups after these exclusions,
removing another 212 offers. Declined includes unselected competitors when a
different option was selected; it does not identify deliberate rejection.

receive equal weight. The interval conditions on the frozen 50-cluster

with one and five seconds as fixed sensitivities. It is not a validated attention
threshold. Duration sums observed visible episodes of the entire menu, not gaze
at an individual option. Long unmarked offers remain in the denominator.

the first item as exposed by default. This default policy is hypothetical because
the historical interface configuration is not authenticated. The alternative
domain-limited policy is separately reported. No hover is not no exposure; even
a recorded target is not proof of reading. This human CoAuthor process-record
comparison uses frozen model embeddings to label repertoire and an exact program
to read events; it contains no human attention or preference judgments.

### S15-DRIVE-V1-PHASE0 - complete outcome calibration and storage recovery

**Hypothesis.** Can the unchanged Phase 0 prediction pipeline detect known
personal effects, while refusing a personal-effect claim when no effect is planted?
**METHOD.** Run the complete fixed grid of 150 conditional outcome constructions
on the geometry of 1,399 exposed CoAuthor sessions, 16,855 decisions and 61 writers.
For a random half of writers, shift accept log odds by a constant offset, a
writer-specific content-taste interaction, or recent-choice habit. Use five
fixed magnitudes and ten independent seeds per cell. Redraw all choices, rebuild
resolved-choice lags and refit the original past-only session-start pipeline.
Score four-class half-Brier improvement over its refitted population forecast,
with the frozen 2,000-draw writer-cluster interval. These are synthetic outcomes
on fixed human-record covariates, read by fitted programs; no new human evidence.

Each row is one injection type and accept-log-odds magnitude, with ten fixed
worlds. Recovery means the writer-cluster 95% interval for backbone improvement
over the refitted population forecast is wholly above zero. The fourth column
is the 95% Wilson interval for that ten-world recovery rate. The final column
counts intervals containing the conditional expected gain of the fitted forecasts.

| Injection | Log-odds magnitude | Recovered worlds | Recovery-rate uncertainty | Conditional-target coverage |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| Content-dependent taste | 0 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Content-dependent taste | 0.1 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Content-dependent taste | 0.2 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Content-dependent taste | 0.4 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Content-dependent taste | 0.8 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Recent-choice habit | 0 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Recent-choice habit | 0.1 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Recent-choice habit | 0.2 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Recent-choice habit | 0.4 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Recent-choice habit | 0.8 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 9/10 |
| Constant accept offset | 0 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Constant accept offset | 0.1 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Constant accept offset | 0.2 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Constant accept offset | 0.4 | 0/10 | 0.0% to 27.8% | 10/10 |
| Constant accept offset | 0.8 | 10/10 | 72.2% to 100.0% | 10/10 |

**Found.** The unchanged Phase 0 pipeline recovers the largest constant accept
offset in all ten worlds; no other planted cell meets its recovery criterion.
None of the thirty zero-injection worlds is recovered. **Means.** This instrument
can detect the largest tested stable offset, but sensitivity is not established
for smaller offsets, content-dependent tastes or recent-choice habits on this
fixed grid. The first observed 80% grid crossing is 0.8 for the constant offset;
none is reached for the other constructions. Ten successes have a Wilson lower
bound of 72.2%, so they do not establish an underlying recovery rate of at least
80%. No smooth detection boundary or untested crossing is inferred.

Known injected gain differs from the fitted pipeline's expected gain. At the
largest constant offset, oracle gain spans 0.006984 to 0.013707 half-Brier, while
the fitted conditional gain spans 0.002192 to 0.004294. For the largest content
injection those ranges are 0.005423 to 0.011184 and -0.001308 to 0.000407; for the
largest habit injection they are 0.000786 to 0.001820 and -0.000929 to -0.000200.
The full ranges and observed-minus-expected quantiles for every cell are retained
in the aggregate receipt. Conditional-target coverage is 149/150, a coarse
diagnostic rather than a guarantee about fresh fitted-data intervals. Zero
recoveries in a ten-world null cell still has a 27.8% Wilson upper bound.

The conditional construction fixes text, timing and cohort geometry. The reader
and fitting specification, chosen injection forms and exposed data limit transfer.
This does not identify why a past human contrast was weak, license a human-value
claim, validate the separate text/adaptation or process-identity arms, or justify
retrofitting earlier intervals. Those arms remain unbuilt. No extension, new seed,
new model/provider call or downstream scientific admission follows from this landing.

**Verification and recovery.** All 605 completion-bound files and 600 compressed
world files verify. Decompression matches every raw hash; all 120 reused worlds
match their original files. Construction, full prediction support, fit chronology,
population/personal baseline predictions and all saved statistics independently
reconcile. Bootstrap replay uses cluster sums and counts, independently of the
runner's concatenation implementation; maximum statistic difference is
3.83e-18. The optimizer was not refitted during validation.
All 503 source/input pins and 21 research locks pass. The attempt retains
6,080,100,043 bytes below its 10,737,418,240-byte cap. The
predecessor's lifetime plus successor elapsed time remains below the original
computation allowance. Original failed evidence is preserved. Native exit, released
leases and actual watcher delivery verify. No drive worker remains; reader recovery
is still held below its fixed GPU-memory floor. No new tests harvested this pass.

Curator roll-up: instrument validity; Which planted personal effects can the
Phase 0 pipeline recover?; **Infrastructure**; The largest constant offset is
recovered while the other tested injection cells do not meet the recovery criterion;
project meaning: sensitivity is specific to effect form and scale, with no human
claim; next engineering obligation: retain these limits in downstream interpretation
and implement separate target-matched constructions before other V1 arms;
public scientific claims unchanged; curator decision required: No; detail:

### S15-DRIVE-V2 - complete decomposition of saved forecasts

**Hypothesis.** Does saved forecast error reflect calibration mismatch or weak
discrimination beyond the fitted behavioral baseline? **METHOD.** Decompose the
exact half-Brier loss (half the summed squared probability error, lower is better)
for every frozen forecast, with merged decile and exact-vector bins. Keep the
whole Phase 0 cohort separate from the smaller Stage 14 reader cohort. Invalid
reader answers retain system loss one; probability decompositions use valid rows
only. Recompute all source scores independently, check each bin denominator and
reconstruction, and retain writer-bootstrap intervals conditional on saved fits.

The table reports all 26 arms. Phase 0 uses 16,855 decisions from 61 writers;
reader arms use 234 decisions from 31 writers. Population means the pooled prior,
personal means the writer-frequency prior, and backbone means the frozen fitted
behavioral model. H0 is no history, H1 earlier same-session choices, H2 earlier
own-session histories, and H3 matched other-writer histories. BCTS is class-bias
and temperature calibration; EM+T is the requested expectation-maximization
prior correction then temperature scaling, whose label-shift assumptions remain
unverified. Corrected uses the calibrated reader; stacked combines it with the
backbone and its frozen invalid-answer fallback. Loss is system half-Brier;
Rel and Res are empirical calibration error and resolution on valid rows;
Residual includes within-bin forecast/outcome covariance. Gain is reference loss
minus system loss; positive favors the row. Brackets are 95% writer-resampled
intervals, 2,000 draws, not selection-adjusted. The reference is population in
Phase 0 and backbone in the reader cohort. No cohorts are pooled.

**Found.** The complete decomposition preserves the earlier outcome: none of the
eight calibrated combinations reaches the declared useful gain of 0.01 over
the backbone; every interval's upper bound is below that margin. Raw reader
forecasts have substantial calibration error. The Phase 0 backbone gains 0.023962
[0.017497, 0.030691] over the population forecast. **Means.** Recalibrating or
combining these saved reader outputs has not recovered useful additional
prediction on this exposed cohort. This is a diagnostic of retained fits, not
an independent replication or a general limit on reading makers. Empirical
resolution depends on binning; singleton exact-vector bins can appear maximally

**Hypothesis.** Can the exact trained profile predictor use informative
descriptions without producing an unacceptable advantage from uninformative
descriptions or dependence on option order?
**METHOD.** Inspect Ghost's complete twenty-world study of eight constructed
writers with four decisions each. Verify the exact archived feature/fitting
functions, canonical engine, source archive and dependency bindings, and all
304 scientific files in original and fresh-process replay. Independently
reconstruct all 1,920 targets and their three-arm forecasts, strict chronology,
probability validity, 112 cold starts, world-level paired half-Brier gains and
controls. Exercise the actual failed-witness admission refusal and negative
operator-review launcher refusal without starting a human attempt.

The table reports mean reduction in half-Brier loss (half the squared probability
error) from the own-description predictor against the stated comparator.
Positive values favor own descriptions. Descriptive two-sided Student t 95%
intervals use twenty independent whole-world means, not individual choices.
Planted lower bounds must exceed 0.005; null upper bounds must be at most 0.005.

| Constructed condition and comparator | Mean improvement | 95% interval | Frozen criterion |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Planted description versus task baseline | 0.072071 | 0.042065 to 0.102077 | Pass |
| Planted description versus donor description | 0.062265 | 0.036914 to 0.087616 | Pass |
| Uninformative description versus task baseline | 0.004690 | -0.021710 to 0.031090 | Fail |
| Uninformative description versus donor description | -0.005608 | -0.019236 to 0.008020 | Fail |
| Constant description versus task baseline | 0.004472 | 0.003281 to 0.005663 | Fail |
| Constant description versus donor description | 0.000000 | 0.000000 to 0.000000 | Pass |

**Found.** The complete dependency witness is FAIL. The uninformative intervals
are too wide to certify the frozen null bound; this does not establish a positive
false advantage. The constant-feature baseline difference is consistent with a
changed effective prior, but its mechanism is not identified here. Option-order
invariance fails in four worlds (3, 7, 13 and 16); the maximum forecast difference
is 6.83209028163e-6 against the fixed 1e-7 tolerance. Future-label prefix changes
and constant own/donor forecasts differ by exactly zero. Strict training-ID,
coverage and probability checks pass. Original and fresh-process replay agree;
the scientific packet used 2,221.90625 CPU seconds across both passes, with
companion review/helper accounting separate. No new p-value is introduced.

**Means.** The prepared human comparison remains unrun: a completed failed
witness cannot satisfy its gate. This is a constructed instrument limitation,
not negative human predictive evidence or a general failure of profiles.
Four decisions per writer do not exercise later personal-penalty calibration;
supplied descriptions do not validate model-generated profile fidelity. Preserve
the original attempt, criteria and canonical capsule. The bounded next obligation
is canonical diagnosis of option-order sensitivity and constant-feature behavior,
then a separately frozen matching witness with adequate null precision and
calibration-branch coverage. Do not tune thresholds or keep rerunning this study
until it passes. Independent local reader work continues.

### S15-SCOPE-DIAGNOSTIC-ENDPOINT - explicit target scoping is not a general repair

**Hypothesis.** Can explicit target-sentence instructions prevent the local
person and theme readers from using surrounding context incorrectly?
**METHOD.** Cross 32 constructed target sentences with absent, matching and
conflicting context, using either the canonical prompt or the same prompt with
an explicit target-field instruction. Repeat all 192 conditions byte-identically
in a second shuffled pass. Independently reconstruct every request, parse every
whole response, recompute all correctness/context/repeat contrasts and verify
frozen sources, raw evidence, CPU residency and native closure.

**Found.** Explicit target scoping is not a general repair. Grammatical-person
accuracy worsens; theme accuracy improves in some conditions while losing the
ability to return the correct empty set. The table reports correct answers out
of 32 calls per row/arm: 16 distinct targets, each repeated twice. Theme scoring
requires the exact tag set. These are constructed conditions, not independent
human observations or a new admission battery.

| Question | Surrounding context | Original prompt, correct / attempted | Explicit target prompt, correct / attempted |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Grammatical person | Absent | 30 / 32 | 9 / 32 |
| Grammatical person | Matching target class | 22 / 32 | 16 / 32 |
| Grammatical person | Conflicting target class | 32 / 32 | 16 / 32 |
| Literal themes | Absent | 18 / 32 | 24 / 32 |
| Literal themes | Matching target class | 24 / 32 | 18 / 32 |
| Literal themes | Conflicting target class | 10 / 32 | 14 / 32 |

The frozen prompt-by-context contrast subtracts the prompt gain under matching
context from its gain under conflicting context. It is -31.25 percentage points
for person and +31.25 points for themes. The positive theme contrast includes a
loss under matching context; it is not a broad accuracy rescue. Empty-theme
targets go from 24/24 correct with the original prompt to 0/24 with explicit
scope. First-person and mixed-person targets each have 0/24 correct under the
explicit prompt. All per-class cells remain in the aggregate receipt.

Relative to absent context, the original person reader changes answers in 8/32
matching-context calls and 2/32 conflicting-context calls; explicit scope changes
13/32 and 9/32 respectively. For themes those counts are 12/32 and 12/32 with
the original prompt, versus 10/32 and 16/32 with explicit scope. Context sensitivity
does not by itself establish that the model copied the context's label.

All 384 responses have valid formats. Identical request bodies nevertheless give
different parsed answers in one of 96 person pairs and four of 96 theme pairs.
Temperature zero and the fixed seed therefore did not make this runtime perfectly
repeatable. All 1,920 wire/evidence files, 127 source pins and 384 model/runtime/
CPU-residency records verify. The worker finished in 45 minutes 12.5 seconds,
exited normally, unloaded the model and released its exact lease. Resource floors
and current watcher delivery pass. No provider calls or new spending.

**Means.** Keep Q6/Q10 disabled. This exact clarification introduces new errors
and cannot be adopted as a general fix. The paired test reveals prompt/context
sensitivity and repeat instability; it does not identify a unique mechanism or
invalidate the whole reader program. The selected four theme classes, small
template set and constructed labels limit transfer. Any future repair needs its
own complete admission battery and natural-data/scientific prerequisites; no
post-hoc class salvage, threshold change or automatic retry follows here.
Stage 15 remains open for its previously gated comparisons. The other questions'
constructed dispositions and all original failures remain unchanged. No new
tests harvested on this operational wake; the finite addendum queue is drained.

### S15-HISTORY-TEXTURE-V1 - matched writers do not show a monotone history curve

**Hypothesis.** Does the history-length pattern survive comparing the same writers?
**METHOD.** Re-score all retained chronological forecasts without fitting or
model calls. Compare equal-writer mean gains in adjacent history bins, restricting
each contrast to writers represented in both bins. Repeat for writer-novel and
globally novel prompts, and both population and personal-frequency baselines.
Independent scalar arithmetic verifies every support count, sign count and contrast.

**Found.** The matched history curve is not monotone. Improvements over population
frequencies coexist with a smaller, irregular advantage over personal-frequency
predictions. The table reports complete all-decision contrasts. A gain is the
comparator's half-Brier probability loss minus the backbone's loss; a positive
late-minus-early difference means the backbone's relative advantage grows.
Writer count is the common support of each adjacent pair, not a new sample.

| Prior own decisions, early to late | Same writers | Change versus population frequencies | Change versus personal frequencies |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 to 1-9 | 31 | -0.00719 | -0.00424 |
| 1-9 to 10-29 | 26 | +0.01181 | -0.01533 |
| 10-29 to 30-99 | 40 | +0.00361 | -0.00186 |
| 30-99 to 100-299 | 26 | +0.00724 | +0.00143 |
| 100-299 to 300+ | 14 | +0.00032 | +0.00065 |

All 16,855 decisions from 61 writers remain accounted for. Only six writers span
all six bins; the writer-novel balanced curve has three. Globally novel prompts
have no matched writers in the first three adjacent contrasts and only one in
each of the last two, so they cannot support a general history-learning curve.
All subsets, both baselines, zero-support cells, balanced curves and leave-one-writer-out
ranges are retained in the receipt. There are no new significance tests or
confirmatory decisions. The independent check verifies 202 scalar comparisons.

**Means.** Writer composition alone does not explain every change, but more
history does not guarantee a steadily growing advantage. Task mix, time, growth
of the population training set and selective continuation remain confounded.
This is an exploratory description of historically exposed forecasts, not a causal
history-dose experiment or new human-mechanism evidence. The next useful scientific
comparison keeps a strong personal-frequency baseline and tests incremental
own-profile information against donor profiles under the existing gates.

### S15-FEATURE-BUILD - profile inputs verified; literal admission launched

**Hypothesis.** Can the repaired profiles be supplied as real prediction features,
and can the literal reader be tested against known answers before scientific use?
**METHOD.** Build matched baseline, own-profile and donor-profile arms on the
pinned canonical ToMpathy predictor. Run planted-relation, null, future-label and
admission-refusal software controls. Independently reconstruct every prepared
matrix from retained source targets, history, profile text and fixed hashing.
Separately test and launch eight complete literal-question batteries on one CPU
inference thread, retaining exact input, response, runtime and residency records.

**Found.** The profile comparison is built and its inputs verify; scientific
fitting remains held. All five profile software tests pass, and the independent
reconstruction covers all 234 targets from 31 writers and all 160 source pins.
The three matched feature matrices have four choices and 164 columns; own/donor
matrices differ for every target, labels align and remain separate, and all

### G3-S14-MAKER-MAIN - own cross-session history shows no primary reader advantage

**Hypothesis.** Does a maker's earlier cross-session history help the cloud reader predict later handling of suggestions beyond no history, another maker's history, personal class frequencies and a cheap partial-pooling model?

**METHOD.** Complete the frozen Qwen3.5 27B Q4_K_M Modal main on 234 later suggestion-handling opportunities from 31 writers and 20 fixed prompts, excluding all three pilot writers. Four evidence arms make 936 calls: no history, earlier decisions in the same session, the maker's earlier cross-session decisions and another maker's earlier decisions. Compare their saved probabilities with the seven already fitted local handling baselines on identical target keys. Primary loss is half of the multiclass Brier score, averaged within writer and then equally across writers; invalid replies cost one. Pair all contrasts within writer, use 10,000 writer bootstrap resamples and two-sided sign flips with a plus-one correction, and retain crossed writer/prompt bootstrap sensitivity. Holm correction retains all eleven frozen primary slots; the five unavailable Opus tests occupy conservative unit slots without being reported as observed p-values. Reconstruct the full source data and every native prompt, verify all archives, source pins, residency and ended ownership, replay independent arithmetic/calibration and rerun the saved-output consumer without inference. Analysis implementation details were frozen and known-answer tested after collection but before this main scoring; no outcome selects a roster, model, control or next run.

The table shows the six available primary half-Brier contrasts. Gain is rival loss minus reader loss, so positive favors the reader. Writer and crossed writer/prompt columns are 95% bootstrap intervals; raw p is the two-sided writer sign-flip probability and Holm p adjusts across all eleven commissioned contrasts. The other five, for Opus, are unavailable.

| Reader evidence | Rival | Gain | Writer interval | Crossed interval | Raw p | Holm p (11) |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| Same-session history | Population frequency | -0.052482 | [-0.087291, -0.017811] | [-0.118381, 0.018189] | 0.007399 | 0.059194 |
| Own cross-session history | Population frequency | -0.078032 | [-0.127322, -0.036352] | [-0.137694, 0.009163] | 0.000100 | 0.001100 |
| Own cross-session history | Other-maker history | -0.002207 | [-0.059362, 0.049326] | [-0.065989, 0.099290] | 0.943506 | 1.000000 |
| Own cross-session history | No history | 0.039965 | [-0.005489, 0.082221] | [-0.022267, 0.139080] | 0.079292 | 0.555044 |
| Own cross-session history | Personal frequency | -0.080962 | [-0.119201, -0.045748] | [-0.139314, -0.002333] | 0.000100 | 0.001100 |
| Own cross-session history | Partial-pooling model | -0.093760 | [-0.142058, -0.053707] | [-0.150998, -0.006920] | 0.000100 | 0.001100 |

**Found.** No primary predictive advantage is established for the own-history reader. Its difference from other-maker history is unresolved, as is its improvement over no history. It performs worse than population frequency, personal frequency and partial pooling under writer resampling and the eleven-slot Holm correction; the crossed prompt sensitivity retains the disadvantages to personal frequency and partial pooling, but includes zero against population frequency. Same-session history is worse than population frequency under the unadjusted writer interval, but its Holm result and crossed interval are unresolved. These findings concern this frozen reader and evidence construction; they do not establish that personal information is absent or that makers are interchangeable.

**Log loss and calibration.** On the same 232 valid own-history targets, the gain over population frequency is -0.254982 nats (writer interval [-0.396790, -0.126313]) and over personal frequency is -0.251306 ([-0.372772, -0.132407]). The full-support sensitivity assigning invalids -log(0.01) gives -0.288724 and -0.287034 respectively. Baseline probabilities are unchanged, and no valid-only mean is subtracted from an unmatched baseline mean. These are baseline-relative log-loss gains, not exact predictive V-information. Calibration uses ten literal bins and the probability assigned to the stated choice, with equal writer weight on valid support. One same-session response chooses a nonmaximal-probability class; its actual choice is retained for accuracy and calibration. Invalids count as incorrect in system accuracy, remain in system loss and have no invented calibration confidence. All class marginals, bin counts, paired log-loss sensitivities and descriptive contrasts are retained in the aggregate results.

**Support and limits.** Twenty-seven writers have eight targets, two have five, one has seven and one has one; equal-writer weighting is retained. Observed classes are 121 accept, 52 edit, 56 dismiss and five ignore. Own histories contain sixteen decisions for 26 writers, twelve for three and eight for two. Donor histories range from eight to twenty-three decisions because the frozen construction matches rendered character length; four main donors miss the 15% ratio band. Full-sixteen sensitivity retains 26 writers/201 targets; matched donor length retains 27/202; both retain 22/169. Own versus donor remains unresolved in all three, and the subsets do not establish an own-history advantage. The frozen exposure roster positively witnesses eighteen targets; the Stage 14 supplement witnesses thirty-three, with forty-six in their union and 188 unknown. Missing witnesses never imply untouched evidence. These public human process records and GPT-3 suggestions may also have appeared in model pretraining. Writer bootstrap and sign-flip inference assume writer independence that shared histories/donors do not establish; crossed prompt resampling does not repair that shared-evidence dependence. The prompts are fixed, profile/effort API comparisons are unavailable, and this is neither a causal preference-strength estimate nor a human value-identification test.

**Validity and accounting.** All 2,345 archive members, 23 frozen launch bindings, 936 native prompt/wire reconstructions, 468 residency records and exact returned prompt-token counts verify. The entire prepared data build reconstructs from 2,892 source bindings, including exclusions and chronology. The exposure supplement's 161 bindings verify. Ten responses contain a zero probability below the frozen floor; no clipping, repair or reask occurs. Invalid counts are three without history, four with same-session history, two with own cross-session history and one with donor history. The maximum cumulative invalid fraction at completed concurrency groups is 3.846%, below the frozen 5% stop threshold. Six targeted known-answer and serialization tests pass; independent score arithmetic, stated-choice calibration and byte-stable consumer reentry pass. Reentry exposed integer histogram keys that become strings in JSON. The original consumer and first outputs are preserved; a separately pinned successor changes only histogram serialization and its record version. All predictions, per-writer values and reported statistics match the original exactly; independent source reconstruction and byte-stable successor reentry pass. Native supervision exits and the provider app is stopped. Measured allocation is 6,963.564 seconds; the main reservation reconciles from $13.40 to a conservative $4.76, pending final invoice. Combined campaign booking is $5.48, including both Modal runs and the failed API profile pilot.

The local reader-runtime hold and failed SM4 admission also remain. No tests were harvested from this operational wake. **Means.** Keep constructed extraction admission separate from natural forecast and complete-graph admission. Independent personal and CPU families continue.

**Curator roll-up.** Theory group: measurement validity. Question: Does the extraction-admitted local reader also give usable natural handling forecasts beyond a cheap prior? Project meaning: Keep constructed extraction admission separate from natural forecast and complete-graph admission. Independent personal and CPU families continue. ### S14-D01 - bounded source-stream detector completes with underpowered rare-error claims

**Hypothesis.** Can lexical features distinguish human-typed fragments from accepted model offers on held writers beyond fixed length and shuffled labels?

### L460 - matched memory changes the recorded-action forecast, without an overall memory benefit

**Hypothesis.** Linking the same retrieved facts to their recorded roles improves a model reader's support for the actual handling of a writing suggestion beyond raw facts or repetition.

**METHOD.** Run the separately frozen matched-memory repair on all 68 original exposed CoAuthor episodes: four development, eight calibration and fifty-six reserve records, each with two nominal evidence views and seven conditions. The original GPT-2-medium reader assigns conditional likelihoods to the same five ordered action labels. Both raw and linked memory contain the identical declared projection of one retrieved training episode from a separate connected source component: handling, endpoint excerpt, slot, actor, operation, relation and exact spans. Rendering round trips preserve these fields; supplemental span identifiers, span-state labels and related-slot metadata are absent from both. The main conditions have equal native-token length within each episode/view, with explicit padding; unpadded raw facts measure padding sensitivity. Repeat raw memory exactly, cyclically misassociate the same fact bundles, provide irrelevant context, or omit memory as controls. Evidence is the first 200 native tokens of the original bounded projection; every complete prompt stays within 960 native tokens. No new source selection, fitting, threshold selection or neural repeats occur during the audit.

**Validity.** All seventeen producers pass their immutable bindings and full cases-by-views-by-conditions census. Saved native prompt fingerprints and token lengths match full-roster admission; truths, original model identity, individual row files and candidate likelihoods verify. The complete 952-row consumer reproduces exactly. Independent probability reconstruction, categorical loss arithmetic, means and paired differences agree for all 252 reported statistics. Every partition contains only one connected source component, so all population intervals remain unavailable. Sixty-one of sixty-eight nominal view pairs have identical native prompts and predictions across every condition; the two views are not independent replications.

The table gives complete descriptive means for every partition and condition. A is the artifact projection; C nominally adds prior text and offered alternatives, subject to the declared evidence clipping. Log loss is negative natural log probability assigned to the true action (lower is better). Brier loss is summed squared probability error over the five labels (lower is better); accuracy is the fraction whose most probable label is correct (higher is better). One source component per partition means these are episode means within that component, not population estimates.

| Partition | Memory condition | A log loss | A Brier loss | A accuracy | C log loss | C Brier loss | C accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Development | No memory | 2.022961 | 0.936597 | 0.000000 | 2.022961 | 0.936597 | 0.000000 |
| Development | Raw facts, padded | 2.485247 | 1.154731 | 0.000000 | 2.485247 | 1.154731 | 0.000000 |
| Development | Linked facts, padded | 1.974561 | 1.043278 | 0.000000 | 1.974561 | 1.043278 | 0.000000 |

| Calibration | No memory | 1.323947 | 0.675672 | 0.375000 | 1.340658 | 0.694495 | 0.375000 |
| Calibration | Raw facts, padded | 1.788259 | 0.930968 | 0.250000 | 1.806278 | 0.945825 | 0.250000 |

| Calibration | Misassociated facts | 1.586342 | 0.861224 | 0.250000 | 1.605281 | 0.877945 | 0.250000 |
| Calibration | Irrelevant context | 1.385185 | 0.688813 | 0.375000 | 1.404675 | 0.707292 | 0.250000 |
| Calibration | Raw facts, unpadded | 1.634553 | 0.833504 | 0.250000 | 1.654992 | 0.856059 | 0.250000 |
| Reserve | No memory | 1.476157 | 0.704491 | 0.464286 | 1.474311 | 0.703742 | 0.446429 |
| Reserve | Raw facts, padded | 1.810588 | 0.855993 | 0.285714 | 1.826837 | 0.865080 | 0.285714 |
| Reserve | Linked facts, padded | 1.511606 | 0.737648 | 0.357143 | 1.520327 | 0.742578 | 0.357143 |
| Reserve | Repeated raw facts | 1.756194 | 0.849532 | 0.267857 | 1.771414 | 0.860033 | 0.267857 |
| Reserve | Misassociated facts | 1.567704 | 0.769781 | 0.357143 | 1.582114 | 0.777537 | 0.357143 |
